text:
maria.k: Heads-up: Acme reported a steady p95 increase on our hosted text-gen endpoint starting ~02:10 UTC. Their customer-facing SLOs hit hard. Can infra triage?

dan.h: Seen similar alerts on eu-west. Correlating with last night's cuda-driver rollout and a small GPU firmware patch.

simon_r: Adding logs/traces now. Initial signal: tail latency increases on kernel preemptting evict paths + NVMe queue depth spikes.

jessica: Customer says errors are retries and timeouts (HTTP 504) during high-concurrency training calls, not auth. But CS reported some token refresh flakiness earlier — unclear relation.

maria.k: @cs-triage, put Acme on priority support list; send workaround routing to dedicated us-east pool if possible.

cs-triage: Confirmed. I gave them a temporary key scoped to dedicated capacity and reduced concurrency limits on their account. They see immediate drop in p95 but still some 2-3x above baseline.

ops-bot: deploy-notification: cuda-driver-532.10 rolled out to eu-west-1 nodes 01:50 UTC; gpu-fw-1.2.7 applied to a subset 01:58 UTC.

dan.h: Repro steps I'm running:
```
# repro load (lightweight):
ab -n 2000 -c 50 http://gateway/eu-west/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
# monitor iostat + dmesg on node
watch -n1 iostat -x 1
journalctl -f -u redwood-agent
```

simon_r: Raw metrics: NVMe avg qdepth baseline 4 -> spiking to 80 under load; host kernel preempt_count rising; context-switches jump. KV-cache hit doesn't change meaningfully.

jessica: Could this be the CUDA driver changes interacting with host kernel scheduler causing longer io completion latency? We've seen similar with previous minor driver/firmware combos.

dan.h: Likely. I started a bisect: nodes with older driver+fw keep baseline p95; upgraded nodes show regression.

maria.k: Mitigation options? Immediate: route Acme's requests away from upgraded nodes, rollback driver on a small pool, or enable sync batching limits.

simon_r: Quick mitigation I pushed to canary: set request-routing policy to prefer nodes with tag cuda-531. Rolled to 10% of traffic; p95 for Acme fell ~40% within 3 mins.

jessica: Good. For customer-facing mitigation we should: 1) keep Acme on dedicated pool; 2) throttle their concurrent requests to 25; 3) keep routing preference to older-driver nodes until patch or kernel tweak.

dan.h: For infra fix: options are rollback driver on eu-west pool, or tune kernel preempt and NVMe scheduler parameters (mq-deadline -> none adjustments), or ask GPU vendor about fw interplay. I'll open a rollback play if PM approves.

maria.k: PM approved emergency rollback for affected clusters. @ops-bot start rollback playbook eu-west-1 group-alpha.

ops-bot: playbook-started: rollback-driver-eu-west-1-group-alpha by dan.h at 1749955220. Steps: cordon -> drain -> package-reinstall -> validation. ETA ~30m.

simon_r: Collecting validation checks to run post-rollback: 
- p95/p99 token latency from real-customer traces
- NVMe qdepth histograms
- dmesg for device timeouts
- container OOM/scheduler events

dan.h: After partial rollback (10 nodes), early signals: qdepth back to ~6, p95 trending toward baseline. Holding rollout paused for confirmation.

jessica: Also noticed a handful of 401s earlier from token refresher hitting auth-db timeouts during the spike. Might have been collateral due to resource contention. CS cleared auth once traffic lowered. Not primary cause but worth monitoring.

maria.k: Action items:
- dan.h: finish rollback and run sim load tests, capture perf diffs (1749955100 -> 1749955285).
- simon_r: collect and attach the kernel+nvme traces and KV-cache telemetry for postmortem.
- jessica: keep Acme updated and keep them on dedicated pool; monitor auth refresh errors.
- cs-triage: create support ticket with customer notes + mitigations.

cs-triage: Ticket #SUP-1876 created; included temporary key details and mitigation steps. Customer thanked us for fast response. :thumbsup:

dan.h: Rollback completed on group-alpha at 1749955255. Validation run in progress. Early p95 numbers: baseline 220ms -> after rollback 240ms -> previously degraded nodes were 950-1200ms. Good.

simon_r: Attaching short snippet of dmesg during the spike for posterity:
```
[Feb 12 02:12:34] nvme0: I/O timeout, aborting cmd
[Feb 12 02:12:34] nvme0: failed command: read
[Feb 12 02:12:34] nvme0: abort status: 0x1
[Feb 12 02:12:35] Kernel: preempt_count high: 1024
```

jessica: I'll schedule a postmortem thread and tag vendor support for a deeper driver/fw interaction analysis. Recommend we block further cuda-driver-532.* rollouts until vendor confirms compatibility.

maria.k: Agreed. Also add an automated routing check to prefer older-driver nodes for critical customers during rollout windows.

dan.h: Follow-up: I'll draft a short runbook for future rollouts (include quick bisect scripts, routing toggles, and rollback steps).

simon_r: Will store traces in S3 under s3://redwood-incident-traces/1749955100/ for the postmortem.

ops-bot: incident-closure-suggested: rollback validated; customer on dedicated pool; monitoring stable for 10m.

maria.k: Closing: keep monitoring for 2h and then schedule PM-led postmortem. Great cross-team response, everyone. :heart:
